instructions.mission: Implement story tasks for Epic {epic_num} Story {story_num}
instructions.critical: Execute continuously without pausing. Do NOT stop for milestones or progress updates.

steps.step:
Load the story file and extract all tasks, acceptance criteria, and developer notes.
Also parse: - Testing Requirements section (unit tests, negative tests, integration tests) - Quality Gates section (lint, type check, build, tests, runtime verification) - Any existing "Senior Developer Review" section from prior reviews
Note all BLOCKING quality gate checkboxes that must be satisfied before completion.

Load project context for coding standards, patterns, and conventions.
Identify: - Architecture docs and coding standards - Existing patterns and conventions in the codebase - Testing patterns already used in the project - Library documentation (if provided in context) — use for correct API usage, method signatures, and up-to-date patterns

Examine project root for build system files (package.json, pyproject.toml, pom.xml, build.gradle, Cargo.toml, Makefile) and determine commands for lint, typecheck, build, and test. Store detected commands for step 6.

Check if the story contains a "Senior Developer Review" section from a prior code-review phase.
If a review section exists: 1. Extract all issues marked with [AI-Review] tags or listed as action items 2. Prioritize fixing these review items BEFORE implementing remaining regular tasks 3. Track which review items are addressed during implementation
If no review section exists, proceed directly to step 5.
IMPORTANT — Prior run artifacts: If source files already exist from a prior failed run, do NOT assume they are correct or complete. Treat them as a starting point that likely has issues. You must still verify every task, fix problems, and run quality gates. Never skip implementation just because files exist.

For each task in the story (review follow-up items first, then regular tasks):
1. Write failing tests first (red) - Create test files if they don't exist - Include both positive and negative test cases - Cover edge cases identified in Testing Requirements 2. Implement the minimum code to pass (green) 3. Refactor for quality (refactor) 4. Verify tests actually exist and pass for this task 5. Immediately update the story file: - Mark task checkbox complete [x] - Mark every Acceptance Criteria satisfied by this task as [x] 6. If addressing a review item, cross-reference the original finding
IMPORTANT: Update checkboxes after EACH task, not at the end. If you skip this, the story will fail code review for incomplete artifact tracking.
For each task, ensure: - Test file exists with real assertions (not placeholders) - Tests cover the negative scenarios from the Testing Requirements checklist - All new tests pass before moving to the next task

Using detected toolchain from step 3, run all quality gates: 1. Lint check → fix failures 2. Type check → fix failures 3. Build → fix failures 4. Full test suite → all tests must pass (new and existing) 5. Integration tests if applicable
Update the story's Quality Gates section with Pass/Fail results. Verify test files exist with real assertions for new/modified modules.
BLOCKING: If ANY gate fails, fix the issue and re-run. Do NOT proceed to completion with failing quality gates.

BEFORE marking the story complete, verify actual work was done: 1. Run git diff --stat to confirm source files were created or modified 2. If no source files were changed, you have NOT completed implementation — go back to step 5
Definition of done: - All acceptance criteria checkboxes marked [x] in the story file - All task checkboxes checked [x] in the story file - All BLOCKING quality gates passing - Testing Requirements checkboxes updated - Quality Gates table updated with Pass/Fail status
Update story file: - Set status to "review" - Update Dev Agent Record with: - Agent Model Used - File List (all created/modified files) - Completion Notes (summary of what was done) - Debug Log References (if any issues encountered) - Update Change Log with summary of changes

Provide a summary of accomplishments:
1. Tasks completed (with count) 2. Tests written (unit, integration, negative scenarios) 3. Quality gate results (all pass/fail status) 4. Files created or modified 5. Any review items addressed (if this was a review continuation)
Suggest: "Story is ready for code-review. Consider running code-review with a different LLM than was used for implementation for best results."
